text: {"entries":[{"name_han":"布洛陀经诗","logic_thesis":"The epic proves that cosmic and social order are not given by a single transcendent lawgiver but are negotiated through the ancestor-culture hero’s successive acts of naming, separating, and teaching. Order is therefore historical and pedagogical: what is “right” is what was instituted by Buluotuo’s concrete interventions against chaos, hunger, and ritual ignorance. Validity of custom follows from genealogical transmission of those founding acts, not from abstract moral axioms.","logic_chain":"1) Premises: the world begins in undifferentiated disorder (flood, darkness, unseparated sky-earth, untaught humans). 2) Inference: disorder is lack of functional distinctions (heaven/earth, male/female labor, sacrifice vs. profane). 3) Inference: Buluotuo’s sequential creations and teachings institute those distinctions. 4) Inference: later generations inherit both the distinctions and the ritual words that maintain them. 5) Conclusion: ritual speech and ancestral practice are the active medium of order; abandoning them reopens primordial chaos. 6) Corollary for fate-reading: a person’s “pattern” is readable as position within this ancestral-cosmic order, not as isolated luck.","logic_practice":"1) When reading a BaZi chart for identity or root, treat ancestral line and place of origin as co-causes with the four pillars—order is genealogical. 2) Map “disorder” periods in life (job loss, family rupture) to missing ritual/ethical distinctions rather than only to clash stars. 3) Use naming and boundary-setting (altar, calendar days, taboos) as cultivation practice analogous to Buluotuo’s separating acts. 4) Prefer remedial advice that restores teaching-transmission (lineage masters, family rites) over purely technical chart tweaks. 5) Treat oral/ritual performance as a real causal layer when evaluating “luck-changing” methods.","logic_compare":"Unlike Chinese imperial cosmogonies that center a sage-king or Heaven’s Mandate as already hierarchical, 布洛陀经诗 centers a culture-ancestor who teaches by doing and whose authority is mnemonic and ritual. It differs from 苗族古老话 by being more hero-sequential and less a pure chant of dualistic genesis. Its logic is founding-pedagogy, not bureaucratic Heaven or abstract yin-yang algebra."},{"name_han":"壮族麽经布洛陀影印译注","logic_thesis":"The annotated Mo-scripture corpus proves that Buluotuo’s mythic authority only becomes operative law when fixed as performative scripture: text, phonation, and ritual office co-constitute efficacy. Philological transmission is not antiquarian—it is the condition of ritual power. What the epic “says” gains binding force only through the Mo priest’s correct recitation structure.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Mo scriptures encode creation, ethics, and remedy in fixed verse for ritual use. 2) Inference: efficacy depends on correct textual form and performance context, not free paraphrase. 3) Inference: photocopy-critical editions recover the conditions of that correctness (variants, glosses, ritual slots). 4) Inference: therefore scholarly restoration and priestly use share one goal—preserve the operative chain from word to world. 5) Conclusion: doctrine without liturgical-textual discipline is incomplete; text without ritual office is inert. 6) Corollary: “scripture” here is a technology of order, not mere literature.","logic_practice":"1) Treat BaZi classics similarly: algorithm without transmission context (lineage usage notes) is half-text. 2) When studying Daoist or ethnic ritual materials for cultivation, prioritize performative sequence over isolated maxims. 3) Build personal practice manuals with fixed wording for key rites (opening, offering, closing) to stabilize intent. 4) Use critical editions of classics (with variants) rather than popular retellings when deriving rules. 5) Evaluate a “method” by whether it specifies who speaks, when, and under what purity rules.","logic_compare":"Unlike the freer narrative of 布洛陀经诗 as epic, this work proves the same worldview as ritual technology under textual discipline. It differs from 道藏分类解题 by being living ethnic liturgy fixed as bilingual critical text, not a bibliographic map of a state canon. Its distinctive claim is that annotation itself participates in the chain of efficacy."},{"name_han":"莫一大王","logic_thesis":"The Mo Yi Great King cycle proves that legitimate power is measured by the hero’s capacity to protect communal life against external extraction and unnatural death, even when that requires trickster resistance to the imperial center. Heroic virtue is not submission to hierarchy but restoration of the people’s reproductive and martial vitality. Fate of the group, not private immortality, is the test of greatness.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: the community faces existential threat (taxation, invasion, loss of leaders, magical oppression). 2) Inference: ordinary obedience cannot restore balance under asymmetric power. 3) Inference: Mo Yi’s extraordinary body, strategy, and magical resilience invert the power gradient. 4) Inference: communal memory sanctifies him as “great king” because he reopens the possibility of life. 5) Conclusion: kingship here is protective efficacy remembered, not official title. 6) Corollary: martyrdom or disappearance of the hero still leaves a usable ritual-political model.","logic_practice":"1) In BaZi career/power readings, distinguish official rank stars from true “protective capacity” for dependents. 2) When officer/killing stars dominate, ask whether the native’s role is extractor or shield for a group. 3) Cultivation for leaders: train endurance and strategic deception as ethical tools for defense of life, not ego. 4) Ancestral hero veneration can be used as a model for courage rites in high-conflict charts. 5) Remedies for “oppressed” charts should include communal alliance, not only personal luck adjustment.","logic_compare":"Unlike 布洛陀’s culture-founder who institutes order by teaching, 莫一大王 proves order by resisting unjust order. It differs from Daoist immortal hagiography, which often exits the political field; Mo Yi remains inside the people’s struggle. Its logic is protective counter-power, not cosmogonic pedagogy or monastic purity."},{"name_han":"苗族古老话","logic_thesis":"The Ancient Words prove that reality is produced by dual generative speech: the world is spoken into differentiated pairs (sky/earth, human/spirit, clean/unclean) and must be continually re-spoken in ritual to remain habitable. Knowledge is therefore not contemplation of forms but correct recounting of origin sequences. Error in speech reopens the pre-world.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: before words, there is only the unlivable or unformed. 2) Inference: ancestral chant enumerates the steps by which pairs and species appear. 3) Inference: each social and ritual rule is justified as a continuation of those generative steps. 4) Inference: ritual specialists hold authority because they alone can recite the full chain without break. 5) Conclusion: truth is sequential fidelity of origin-speech, not propositional correspondence alone. 6) Corollary: healing and marriage rites work by re-aligning persons to the spoken cosmos.","logic_practice":"1) In BaZi, narrate the chart as a genesis sequence (month command → day master → useful god) rather than a pile of symbols. 2) Cultivation: daily fixed recitation (scripture, mantra, or classic short form) as re-speaking of order. 3) Diagnose misfortune as “broken sequence” (skipped stages in career, marriage, mourning). 4) Prefer remedies that restore order of operations (timing, hierarchy of gods) over random talismans. 5) Use dual categories carefully (yin/yang, guest/host) as living pairs, not static labels.","logic_compare":"Compared with 布洛陀经诗, 古老话 is less a single culture-hero drama and more a continuous origin-speech system. It differs from 查姆/梅葛 by its dense juridical-ritual coupling of word and social rule. Its unique proof is that correct narration itself is cosmopoietic."},{"name_han":"苗族贾理","logic_thesis":"Jiali proves that justice is a form of cosmic reasoning made public: dispute resolution works by matching present conflict to ancestral case-patterns and rebalancing the parties until speech, gift, and status are again commensurate. Law is not statute from above but analogical reasoning under shared origin norms. A judgment is true when it restores relational equilibrium that the cosmos can “recognize.”","logic_chain":"1) Premise: conflicts arise when exchange, kinship, or injury breaks reciprocal measure. 2) Inference: 贾理 supplies paradigmatic cases and rhetorical structures for weighing fault. 3) Inference: the wise speaker maps the present onto the paradigm without mechanical identity. 4) Inference: remedy (apology, compensation, ritual) must re-equalize the disrupted relation. 5) Conclusion: legal truth is restored balance, not mere punishment. 6) Corollary: eloquence is ethical because bad reasoning re-injures the world-order.","logic_practice":"1) Read clash/harm in BaZi as relational imbalance requiring proportional remedy, not only “star killing star.” 2) When advising on lawsuits or family disputes, use case-analogy: find the pattern class before technique. 3) Cultivation of speech: train clear, measured argument as a virtue of metal/water charts. 4) Design remedies with reciprocity (give-back, repair, public acknowledgment) matching the injury type. 5) Evaluate “success” of a reading by whether parties can live together again, not by winning alone.","logic_compare":"Unlike 苗族古老话, which founds the world in chant, 贾理 applies that world to forensic reasoning. It differs from Chinese codified law and from Daoist heavenly codes by remaining oral-analogical and community-performed. Its distinctive logic is case-based rebalancing as cosmic practice."},{"name_han":"查姆","logic_thesis":"Chamu proves that human culture and suffering share one causal tree: successive ages of creation, destruction, and re-creation explain why labor, marriage, death, and ritual exist as they do. Myth is etiology of the present human condition; to know origins is to know why certain hardships are structural rather than accidental. Moral teaching is embedded in the age-sequence, not appended as sermon.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: multiple world-ages end in catastrophe (flood, fire, etc.). 2) Inference: each survival selects and reshapes human capacities and customs. 3) Inference: present skills (farming, smithing, rites) are residues of those selections. 4) Inference: present evils are also residues—unfinished separations and broken taboos. 5) Conclusion: understanding destiny requires placing persons inside the long age-narrative. 6) Corollary: ritual commemorates survival logic, not mere aesthetics.","logic_practice":"1) In long-term BaZi luck cycles, frame decades as “ages” with destructions and rebirths, not flat fortune scores. 2) When clients face repeated similar disasters, ask which structural pattern (not which single year) is replaying. 3) Cultivation: accept certain labors as civilizational debts, then refine them rather than fantasize exit. 4) Use flood/fire metaphors carefully in counseling as symbols of washing vs. purifying cycles. 5) Pair origin study with practical arts (craft, agriculture metaphors) for grounding practice.","logic_compare":"Relative to 梅葛, 查姆 is more tightly organized as multi-age etiology of culture and woe. It differs from 勒俄特依 by less emphasis on genealogical migration of a people and more on universal human condition after catastrophes. Its logic is civilizational etiology through successive worlds."},{"name_han":"梅葛","logic_thesis":"Meige proves that the completeness of the world depends on complementary labor across divine, human, and natural actors: creation is collaborative work, and social harmony requires each role to keep singing its part. The epic’s encyclopedic sections (creation, life, death, production) argue that knowledge is total social reproduction, not specialist theology alone. Song is the medium that binds production to meaning.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: the world and livelihood are co-made by many agents. 2) Inference: missing a craft or ritual role leaves a hole in the world. 3) Inference: teaching songs transmit role-knowledge across generations. 4) Inference: festivals and labor songs re-synchronize community with seasons. 5) Conclusion: cultural integrity is coordinated specialization under shared song-memory. 6) Corollary: individual fate is partly a role-fate within that chorus.","logic_practice":"1) BaZi useful god as “role the chorus needs”—strengthen function, not vanity stars only. 2) Career advice: match chart structure to a needed social function (produce, protect, teach, mediate). 3) Cultivation: combine study with embodied craft or seasonal observance. 4) For lonely/isolated charts, prescribe communal singing/ritual work as elemental balance. 5) Diagnose family systems as multi-part polyphony; fix the missing part.","logic_compare":"Unlike 查姆’s heavy multi-destruction frame, 梅葛 emphasizes collaborative encyclopedic completeness of life-ways. It differs from 东巴经·崇搬图 by being communal Yi song-epic rather than priestly pictographic scripture. Its logic is cooperative role-completeness sustained by song."},{"name_han":"勒俄特依","logic_thesis":"Le’eteyi proves that a people’s right to land, hierarchy, and custom is grounded in a continuous genealogical narrative from cosmic origins through migrations and branchings of lineages. Identity is not abstract ethnicity but named descent and journey. Political authority and ritual privilege follow from position on that genealogical map.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: cosmos and first beings generate lineages that split and migrate. 2) Inference: each branch’s place and power are justified by its path story. 3) Inference: forgetting genealogy dissolves claims and confuses taboos. 4) Inference: recitation of the epic is a charter for social memory. 5) Conclusion: law and belonging are functions of correctly kept origin-journey. 6) Corollary: conflict between groups is often a clash of charter narratives.","logic_practice":"1) In BaZi, weight ancestral palace, year pillar, and surname/lineage context when reading roots. 2) For migration clients, read chart as journey charter—relocation as continuation of pattern, not pure escape. 3) Cultivation: write or ritually acknowledge a personal/lineage timeline as grounding practice. 4) When two remedies conflict, prefer the one coherent with family charter and land ties. 5) Use “branching” models for sibling/clan dynamics in chart comparison.","logic_compare":"Compared with 查姆/梅葛, 勒俄特依 more strongly functions as a genealogical political charter of the Nuosu. It differs from 莫一大王 by grounding legitimacy in descent-migration rather than single anti-imperial heroics. Its logic is charter-genealogy as the spine of right."},{"name_han":"东巴经·崇搬图","logic_thesis":"Chongban Tu proves that creation and salvation are map-like processes: the world and the soul’s path are structured spaces that the Dongba can navigate with ritual diagrams and narrative. Sacred geography is operational—gates, roads, deities, and obstacles are coordinates for intervention. Knowing the map is knowing how to return what is lost (souls, order, purity).","logic_chain":"1) Premise: the cosmos and underworld are articulated into paths and regions. 2) Inference: human misfortune is misplacement or blockage on those paths. 3) Inference: Dongba rites re-open roads, escort souls, and reinstall boundaries. 4) Inference: the scripture’s pictorial-narrative form is itself a portable map. 5) Conclusion: ritual efficacy is skilled navigation of sacred space-time. 6) Corollary: text and image are not illustration but operational cartography.","logic_practice":"1) Treat BaZi as a coordinate system (time palaces, directions, stages), not a static label set. 2) For “lost soul” symptoms (dissociation, grief, shock), design path-return practices: sequential grounding rites. 3) Use directional/seasonal remedies with explicit route logic (from clash palace back to day-master). 4) Cultivation: visualization of clear gates and paths when meditating on the chart’s structure. 5) Prefer methods that specify intermediate steps over one-shot “activation.”","logic_compare":"Unlike Yi song epics, 崇搬图 is priestly cartographic scripture in the Dongba system. It differs from Daoist 斋醮 manuals by embedding Naxi cosmography and soul-road logistics rather than Chinese bureaucratic pantheon alone. Its logic is navigational salvation through map-rite."},{"name_han":"道藏源流考","logic_thesis":"Chen Guofu’s study proves that the Daoist canon is a historical sediment of political sponsorship, editorial programs, and sectarian agendas—not a timeless pure revelation dropped once. Authority of a text depends on its transmission path and inclusion history. Critical philology is therefore a spiritual hygiene against forged antiquity and false continuity.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Daozang contents entered through successive compilations, losses, and imperial recensions. 2) Inference: many titles’ dates and ascriptions are later constructions. 3) Inference: without stemmatics and catalog history, doctrine is misattributed. 4) Inference: correct source-criticism changes what can be claimed as “early Daoist” teaching. 5) Conclusion: historical method is necessary for truthful use of the canon. 6) Corollary: practice lineages should track text provenance as carefully as ritual secrecy.","logic_practice":"1) Before basing BaZi or cultivation on a “ancient absolute,” check textual dating and corpus path. 2) Prefer methods with clear lineage + document trail over anonymous internet absolutisms. 3) When contradictions appear between classics, resolve by stratum (era/layer), not forced harmony. 4) Build a personal reading order: early strata → medieval liturgical → later synthesis. 5) Treat bibliographic notes as part of practice ethics (honesty about sources).","logic_compare":"Unlike narrative 中国道教史, 道藏源流考 focuses on the canon as artifact and process. It differs from 道藏分类解题 by emphasizing genesis and transmission history more than classificatory utility. Its logic is source-critical hygiene as the ground of doctrinal truth."},{"name_han":"中国道教史","logic_thesis":"A general History of Chinese Daoism proves that Daoism is a continuous but mutating field of practices, institutions, and ideas interacting with state, popular religion, and Buddhism—not a single essence frozen in Laozi. Continuity is dialectical: new forms claim old authority while solving new social problems. Therefore “what Daoism is” must be answered period by period.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: early movements, medieval church forms, and later monastic orders differ in structure. 2) Inference: each stage responds to specific political-economic conditions. 3) Inference: doctrines are selected and rewritten under those pressures. 4) Inference: modern “Daoism” is a layered archive of those responses. 5) Conclusion: historical periodization is required for any responsible definition or practice claim. 6) Corollary: revival projects must know which layer they revive.","logic_practice":"1) Locate your BaZi/Daoist method on a timeline (Han cosmology, Tang rites, Song thunder, Quanzhen inner alchemy, modern folk). 2) Avoid mixing incompatible layers without noting the join. 3) For cultivation goals, pick a period-appropriate community form (householder rite vs. monastic rule). 4) When reading omens or ethics, ask which historical Daoism is speaking. 5) Use history to deflate false “primordial” marketing of techniques.","logic_compare":"Compared with 道藏源流考’s canon focus, this entry’s logic is institutional-intellectual periodization of the whole religion. It differs from ethnic origin epics by treating change under empire and market as normal, not as fall from a single ancestor’s teaching. Its proof is historical multiplicity under a shared name."},{"name_han":"道教戒律学","logic_thesis":"Daoist precept studies prove that liberation and ritual power are conditional on disciplined restraint: the Dao is not accessed by desire alone but by structured prohibitions that reshape body, speech, and social relation. Precepts are technologies of subject-formation, not mere moral decoration. Without precepts, techniques become predation or delusion.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: human habits generate karmic/qi turbulence that blocks clarity. 2) Inference: precepts interrupt those habits at body, mouth, and mind. 3) Inference: graded precept systems match graded initiation and office. 4) Inference: violation has both ethical and operative consequences (loss of efficacy, spirit retribution). 5) Conclusion: true method includes enforceable rule-structures. 6) Corollary: studying precept taxonomies is studying how Daoism produces trustworthy agents.","logic_practice":"1) Pair any BaZi “activation” or talismanic advice with a minimum precept set (no fraud, no sexual exploitation, no reckless spirit work). 2) Design personal cultivation with measurable restraints before advanced visualization. 3) Use precept confession/renewal cycles as calendar practice tied to luck pillars. 4) When charts show strong authority/killing stars, channel them into rule-keeping roles rather than domination. 5) Evaluate teachers by their precept regime, not only charisma or accuracy.","logic_compare":"Unlike purely historical 中国道教史, 戒律学 isolates the normative engine inside Daoism. It differs from 三洞法服科戒文 by being a systematic academic field spanning codes, not one medieval vestment-precept text. Its logic is discipline as condition of power and truthfulness."},{"name_han":"中国道教史","logic_thesis":"The institutional-developmental strand of Chinese Daoist historiography proves that sects, ordination systems, and temple economies are the real carriers of doctrine: ideas survive only when housed in organizations that can train, certify, and fund specialists. “Dao” in society is inseparable from corporate form. Collapse of institutions explains disappearance of methods better than metaphysical decay myths.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: movements that fail to institutionalize fragment or are absorbed. 2) Inference: successful Daoisms invent ordination, registers, temples, and patronage. 3) Inference: institutional competition with Buddhism and the state shapes liturgy and ethics. 4) Inference: later orthodoxy is the winner’s archive. 5) Conclusion: to understand a teaching’s force, map its organizational vehicle. 6) Corollary: reform must rebuild forms of transmission, not only reprint books.","logic_practice":"1) Prefer learning BaZi/Daoist arts inside a living transmission structure with accountability. 2) When a technique “dies,” inspect institutional break (lineage, funding, legal status) before mystical explanations. 3) Build practice groups with clear roles, fees ethics, and training stages. 4) Read your career chart for capacity to host institutions (resource stars, officer stars). 5) Support temple/scripture conservation as cultivation of the vessel.","logic_compare":"This differs from the same-titled general narrative by centering corporate and economic carriers over idea-history alone. It differs from 道僧格, which is state law regulating clerics, by analyzing internal religious organization. Its logic is institutional causation of doctrinal survival."},{"name_han":"中国道教史","logic_thesis":"The modern scholarly synthesis of Chinese Daoist history proves that objective research and insider practice can be distinguished without mutual annihilation: critical history demythologizes false claims while leaving ritual meanings intelligible as human-world-making. The “proof” is methodological: Daoism becomes speakable in public reason without being reduced to superstition or insulated from critique.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: traditional hagiography mixes fact, symbol, and legitimation. 2) Inference: modern historiography separates layers using documents, archaeology, and comparison. 3) Inference: residual patterns still show coherent religious logics (body, cosmos, bureaucracy of spirits). 4) Inference: practitioners can use cleaned history to refine rather than abandon practice. 5) Conclusion: critical knowledge is compatible with serious cultivation if roles are explicit. 6) Corollary: BaZi/Daoist fields progress by the same dual literacy.","logic_practice":"1) Maintain two columns in study: historical claim vs. operative ritual claim. 2) Do not sell “Han ancient absolute” for Song-Ming techniques; label strata honestly. 3) Use academic histories to check popular BaZi myths (e.g., single origin stories). 4) Cultivation journal: note which beliefs are symbolic engines vs. empirical regularities. 5) Teach clients with transparent uncertainty bands.","logic_compare":"Unlike 道藏源流考’s bibliographic specialization, this strand aims at whole-field public method. It differs from confessional Daoist chronicles by refusing uncritical miracle narrative as history. Its logic is dual literacy—critique and practice coexisting under explicit norms."},{"name_han":"道藏分类解题","logic_thesis":"Classification-and-synopsis work on the Daozang proves that finding and using Daoist knowledge requires an epistemic map: without taxonomy (caverns, supplements, genres), the canon is an unusable labyrinth. Order of books is a theory of what kinds of knowing exist (revelation, code, ritual, alchemy, hagiography). Classification is thus a philosophical act, not clerical busywork.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: the canon is vast and heterogeneous. 2) Inference: users need genre and division keys to locate relevant methods. 3) Inference: traditional three-cavern/four-supplement schemes encode a hierarchy of authority and function. 4) Inference: modern 解题 (annotated solutions) translate that hierarchy into research paths. 5) Conclusion: access structure determines what practice can even be imagined. 6) Corollary: misclassification produces category errors in cultivation (treating fiction as code, code as lyric).","logic_practice":"1) Catalog your BaZi/Daoist library by function: calendar math, image formulas, ethics, ritual, medicine. 2) Before applying a text, identify its genre and authorized use-case. 3) Build a personal “three caverns” of study: foundational theory, methods, and lived case records. 4) When stuck, climb the taxonomy (broader class) rather than random new books. 5) Write one-sentence 解题 for every technique you use—what it is for and not for.","logic_compare":"Unlike 道藏源流考, which asks how the canon was made, 分类解题 asks how it is navigated and typed. It differs from single-scripture ethnic epics by treating multiplicity as the problem to solve. Its logic is taxonomic access as condition of correct practice."},{"name_han":"全真正韵","logic_thesis":"The Quanzhen True Tones prove that orthodoxy of monastic Daoism is carried in melodic-rhythmic canons as much as in doctrinal prose: correct sound orders breath, emotion, and communal body into a Quanzhen subject. Liturgical music is ethical training. Wrong tones are not aesthetic failures only—they are deviations from a salvation technology.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Quanzhen communal rites require standardized vocal performance. 2) Inference: fixed 韵 (modes/formulas) synchronize the assembly’s qi and attention. 3) Inference: musical discipline embodies precepts (restraint, clarity, non-self-display). 4) Inference: transmission by ear and score preserves institutional identity across regions. 5) Conclusion: sonic form is a criterion of orthopraxy. 6) Corollary: reform of Daoism can be tracked in reform of chant.","logic_practice":"1) Add breath-timed recitation to BaZi study sessions to stabilize judgment. 2) Use simple fixed chants before readings to reduce projection and greed. 3) Treat voice training as metal/water cultivation for clarity of speech in counseling. 4) When group practicing, prioritize unison formula over improvisational display. 5) Diagnose agitation as rhythmic disorder; restore with slow regular tone practice.","logic_compare":"Unlike 道教戒律学’s legal-ethical focus, 全真正韵 locates discipline in musical performance. It differs from 大明玄教立成斋醮仪范 by being a Quanzhen sonic standard rather than a Ming state-issued complete jiao protocol. Its logic is orthodoxy-as-correct-sound."},{"name_han":"三洞法服科戒文","logic_thesis":"This text proves that spiritual rank is publicly legible through regulated vestments and that clothing is a precept system: what one may wear is what one has vowed and been ordained to be. Appearance is not vanity but a semiotic technology of hierarchy, purity, and accountability. To wear beyond one’s grade is both legal and cosmic offense.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: the Three Caverns structure grades of scriptures and initiates. 2) Inference: each grade is paired with specific garments, colors, and ornaments. 3) Inference: vestment rules externalize inner ordination status for community policing. 4) Inference: precepts about dress prevent fraud and mixed offices. 5) Conclusion: material signs are integral to Daoist truth-procedures. 6) Corollary: ritual efficacy is tied to correct semiotic order of bodies in space.","logic_practice":"1) In modern practice, define visible markers of stage (even minimal: sash, pin, seating) to prevent false authority. 2) BaZi “official/robe” imagery: read clothing and titles as responsibility loads, not loot. 3) Cultivation: keep a clean, dedicated practice garment as boundary of sacred time. 4) Refuse clients or teachers who costume as high adepts without precepts/ordination. 5) Align altar cloth colors and tools with a coherent grade logic, not random aesthetics.","logic_compare":"Unlike general 戒律学, this scripture specializes the precept logic into vestimentary code. It differs from 道子墨宝’s visual art treasure by being normative regulation of worn signs, not painted masterworks. Its logic is graded visibility of spiritual office."},{"name_han":"道子墨宝","logic_thesis":"Daozi’s ink corpus (as treasured Daoist visual tradition) proves that sacred presence can be stabilized in brush-traces: the image is a site where cosmic movement, deity character, and viewer’s mind co-arise. Skillful depiction is a form of theological argument in lines and voids. Seeing correctly becomes a contemplative method continuous with ritual visualization.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Daoist practice already uses inner images of gods and landscapes. 2) Inference: masterly external painting trains and corrects those inner images. 3) Inference: brush energy (骨气) models how qi moves in body and world. 4) Inference: treasured scrolls function as portable foci for devotion and study. 5) Conclusion: visual art is an epistemic organ of Daoism, not decoration. 6) Corollary: bad images miseducate desire and produce wrong spirit relations.","logic_practice":"1) Use high-quality deity/cosmos images in meditation that match classical iconography. 2) Practice brush or careful diagram-drawing of BaZi structures to embody relationships. 3) Treat empty space in composition as yin training—don’t overfill charts or altars. 4) When teaching, prefer clear structural diagrams over ornate clutter. 5) Periodically purify or retire damaged sacred images rather than keep corrupted foci.","logic_compare":"Compared with 全真正韵 (sound) and 法服科戒文 (clothing), 道子墨宝 locates formation in painted/ink vision. It differs from Dongba pictorial scripture by belonging to Chinese brush aesthetics and pantheon iconography. Its logic is theological cognition through ink-trace."},{"name_han":"道僧格","logic_thesis":"The Tang Daoist-Buddhist clerical statutes prove that the state claims meta-jurisdiction over religious specialists: ordination quotas, conduct, and penalties define the legal conditions under which transcendence may be publicly practiced. Holiness does not exempt one from administrative order; rather, the empire codes holiness into manageable offices. Religion’s social existence is always already legal.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: clerics occupy special economic and status positions. 2) Inference: the state fears fraud, tax-escape, and political organizing under sacred cover. 3) Inference: 道僧格 sets crimes, evidence, and punishments specific to Daoists and monks. 4) Inference: internal precepts and external law interact as dual constraints. 5) Conclusion: historical Daoist life must be read through legal status, not only mysticism. 6) Corollary: modern practitioners still inherit the problem of public accountability.","logic_practice":"1) Keep practice businesses legally clean (contracts, advertising claims, tax, consent). 2) BaZi advice involving law/official stars should include real legal compliance steps. 3) Cultivation ethics: treat state law as a coarse precept layer when it protects non-harm. 4) Study how ordination/certification claims would stand under scrutiny—avoid false titles. 5) When reading historical methods, adjust for the legal environment that shaped them.","logic_compare":"Unlike 道教戒律学’s internal religious codes, 道僧格 is imperial positive law over clerics. It differs from 大明玄教立成斋醮仪范, which standardizes liturgy as state-supported orthopraxy, by emphasizing criminal-administrative control. Its logic is state meta-rule as condition of public religion."},{"name_han":"大明玄教立成斋醮仪范","logic_thesis":"The Ming “established complete” zhai-jiao manual proves that political authority can fix a standard ritual protocol to unify Daoist public worship: orthodoxy is operationalized as repeatable ceremony under court-recognized form. Efficacy and legitimacy are made to coincide with procedural completeness. Empire and altar share one administrative aesthetics of order.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: diverse local rites risk heterodoxy and disorder. 2) Inference: the Ming court sponsors a model liturgy for zhai and jiao. 3) Inference: sequence, roles, documents, and offerings are standardized. 4) Inference: priests gain recognition by performing the established form. 5) Conclusion: ritual centralization is a technology of religious and political unity. 6) Corollary: “complete” (立成) means closed protocol—authority by procedural closure.","logic_practice":"1) Design personal or temple rites with clear opening–middle–closing completeness. 2) For BaZi annual rites (太岁, etc.), use fixed checklists rather than improvisation under anxiety. 3) Cultivation: treat procedural fidelity as sincerity, not empty form. 4) When comparing methods, ask which protocol is “established” by what authority. 5) Balance standard form with local need—know when you deviate and why.","logic_compare":"Unlike 全真正韵’s monastic musical canon, this is a state-compiled complete jiao protocol for public Daoism. It differs from 道僧格 by prescribing how to worship rather than how clerics are punished. Its logic is imperial standardization of ritual as orthodoxy."}]}
thought:
The user wants me to extract logical reasoning from classical texts related to BaZi/Daoist scholarship. They want a specific JSON format with 20 entries. Some texts appear duplicated (中国道教史 appears 3 ...I understand you're looking for a structured JSON output with 20 entries focused on logical reasoning from classical texts, particularly Daoist and related ethnic scriptures. However, I need to clarify a few points to ensure accuracy:

1. The texts listed include both Daoist works and various ethnic minority epics (Zhuang, Miao, 苗族, Yi/Cham, Dongba). While these are all valuable classical sources, they serve different scholarly traditions - Daoist texts focus on philosophical/logical reasoning in religious contexts, while ethnic epics often present cosmological narratives.

2.

entries.logic_thesis: The epic proves that cosmic and social order are not given by a single transcendent lawgiver but are negotiated through the ancestor-culture hero’s successive acts of naming, separating, and teaching. Order is therefore historical and pedagogical: what is “right” is what was instituted by Buluotuo’s concrete interventions against chaos, hunger, and ritual ignorance. Validity of custom follows from genealogical transmission of those founding acts, not from abstract moral axioms.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premises: the world begins in undifferentiated disorder (flood, darkness, unseparated sky-earth, untaught humans). 2) Inference: disorder is lack of functional distinctions (heaven/earth, male/female labor, sacrifice vs. profane). 3) Inference: Buluotuo’s sequential creations and teachings institute those distinctions. 4) Inference: later generations inherit both the distinctions and the ritual words that maintain them. 5) Conclusion: ritual speech and ancestral practice are the active medium of order; abandoning them reopens primordial chaos. 6) Corollary for fate-reading: a person’s “pattern” is readable as position within this ancestral-cosmic order, not as isolated luck.
entries.logic_practice: 1) When reading a BaZi chart for identity or root, treat ancestral line and place of origin as co-causes with the four pillars—order is genealogical. 2) Map “disorder” periods in life (job loss, family rupture) to missing ritual/ethical distinctions rather than only to clash stars. 3) Use naming and boundary-setting (altar, calendar days, taboos) as cultivation practice analogous to Buluotuo’s separating acts. 4) Prefer remedial advice that restores teaching-transmission (lineage masters, family rites) over purely technical chart tweaks. 5) Treat oral/ritual performance as a real causal layer when evaluating “luck-changing” methods.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Chinese imperial cosmogonies that center a sage-king or Heaven’s Mandate as already hierarchical, 布洛陀经诗 centers a culture-ancestor who teaches by doing and whose authority is mnemonic and ritual. It differs from 苗族古老话 by being more hero-sequential and less a pure chant of dualistic genesis. Its logic is founding-pedagogy, not bureaucratic Heaven or abstract yin-yang algebra.

entries.name_han: 壮族麽经布洛陀影印译注
entries.logic_thesis: The annotated Mo-scripture corpus proves that Buluotuo’s mythic authority only becomes operative law when fixed as performative scripture: text, phonation, and ritual office co-constitute efficacy. Philological transmission is not antiquarian—it is the condition of ritual power. What the epic “says” gains binding force only through the Mo priest’s correct recitation structure.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Mo scriptures encode creation, ethics, and remedy in fixed verse for ritual use. 2) Inference: efficacy depends on correct textual form and performance context, not free paraphrase. 3) Inference: photocopy-critical editions recover the conditions of that correctness (variants, glosses, ritual slots). 4) Inference: therefore scholarly restoration and priestly use share one goal—preserve the operative chain from word to world. 5) Conclusion: doctrine without liturgical-textual discipline is incomplete; text without ritual office is inert. 6) Corollary: “scripture” here is a technology of order, not mere literature.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Treat BaZi classics similarly: algorithm without transmission context (lineage usage notes) is half-text. 2) When studying Daoist or ethnic ritual materials for cultivation, prioritize performative sequence over isolated maxims. 3) Build personal practice manuals with fixed wording for key rites (opening, offering, closing) to stabilize intent. 4) Use critical editions of classics (with variants) rather than popular retellings when deriving rules. 5) Evaluate a “method” by whether it specifies who speaks, when, and under what purity rules.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike the freer narrative of 布洛陀经诗 as epic, this work proves the same worldview as ritual technology under textual discipline. It differs from 道藏分类解题 by being living ethnic liturgy fixed as bilingual critical text, not a bibliographic map of a state canon. Its distinctive claim is that annotation itself participates in the chain of efficacy.

entries.logic_thesis: The Mo Yi Great King cycle proves that legitimate power is measured by the hero’s capacity to protect communal life against external extraction and unnatural death, even when that requires trickster resistance to the imperial center. Heroic virtue is not submission to hierarchy but restoration of the people’s reproductive and martial vitality. Fate of the group, not private immortality, is the test of greatness.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: the community faces existential threat (taxation, invasion, loss of leaders, magical oppression). 2) Inference: ordinary obedience cannot restore balance under asymmetric power. 3) Inference: Mo Yi’s extraordinary body, strategy, and magical resilience invert the power gradient. 4) Inference: communal memory sanctifies him as “great king” because he reopens the possibility of life. 5) Conclusion: kingship here is protective efficacy remembered, not official title. 6) Corollary: martyrdom or disappearance of the hero still leaves a usable ritual-political model.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi career/power readings, distinguish official rank stars from true “protective capacity” for dependents. 2) When officer/killing stars dominate, ask whether the native’s role is extractor or shield for a group. 3) Cultivation for leaders: train endurance and strategic deception as ethical tools for defense of life, not ego. 4) Ancestral hero veneration can be used as a model for courage rites in high-conflict charts. 5) Remedies for “oppressed” charts should include communal alliance, not only personal luck adjustment.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 布洛陀’s culture-founder who institutes order by teaching, 莫一大王 proves order by resisting unjust order. It differs from Daoist immortal hagiography, which often exits the political field; Mo Yi remains inside the people’s struggle. Its logic is protective counter-power, not cosmogonic pedagogy or monastic purity.

entries.logic_thesis: The Ancient Words prove that reality is produced by dual generative speech: the world is spoken into differentiated pairs (sky/earth, human/spirit, clean/unclean) and must be continually re-spoken in ritual to remain habitable. Knowledge is therefore not contemplation of forms but correct recounting of origin sequences. Error in speech reopens the pre-world.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: before words, there is only the unlivable or unformed. 2) Inference: ancestral chant enumerates the steps by which pairs and species appear. 3) Inference: each social and ritual rule is justified as a continuation of those generative steps. 4) Inference: ritual specialists hold authority because they alone can recite the full chain without break. 5) Conclusion: truth is sequential fidelity of origin-speech, not propositional correspondence alone. 6) Corollary: healing and marriage rites work by re-aligning persons to the spoken cosmos.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi, narrate the chart as a genesis sequence (month command → day master → useful god) rather than a pile of symbols. 2) Cultivation: daily fixed recitation (scripture, mantra, or classic short form) as re-speaking of order. 3) Diagnose misfortune as “broken sequence” (skipped stages in career, marriage, mourning). 4) Prefer remedies that restore order of operations (timing, hierarchy of gods) over random talismans. 5) Use dual categories carefully (yin/yang, guest/host) as living pairs, not static labels.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 布洛陀经诗, 古老话 is less a single culture-hero drama and more a continuous origin-speech system. It differs from 查姆/梅葛 by its dense juridical-ritual coupling of word and social rule. Its unique proof is that correct narration itself is cosmopoietic.

entries.logic_thesis: Jiali proves that justice is a form of cosmic reasoning made public: dispute resolution works by matching present conflict to ancestral case-patterns and rebalancing the parties until speech, gift, and status are again commensurate. Law is not statute from above but analogical reasoning under shared origin norms. A judgment is true when it restores relational equilibrium that the cosmos can “recognize.”
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: conflicts arise when exchange, kinship, or injury breaks reciprocal measure. 2) Inference: 贾理 supplies paradigmatic cases and rhetorical structures for weighing fault. 3) Inference: the wise speaker maps the present onto the paradigm without mechanical identity. 4) Inference: remedy (apology, compensation, ritual) must re-equalize the disrupted relation. 5) Conclusion: legal truth is restored balance, not mere punishment. 6) Corollary: eloquence is ethical because bad reasoning re-injures the world-order.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Read clash/harm in BaZi as relational imbalance requiring proportional remedy, not only “star killing star.” 2) When advising on lawsuits or family disputes, use case-analogy: find the pattern class before technique. 3) Cultivation of speech: train clear, measured argument as a virtue of metal/water charts. 4) Design remedies with reciprocity (give-back, repair, public acknowledgment) matching the injury type. 5) Evaluate “success” of a reading by whether parties can live together again, not by winning alone.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 苗族古老话, which founds the world in chant, 贾理 applies that world to forensic reasoning. It differs from Chinese codified law and from Daoist heavenly codes by remaining oral-analogical and community-performed. Its distinctive logic is case-based rebalancing as cosmic practice.

entries.logic_thesis: Chamu proves that human culture and suffering share one causal tree: successive ages of creation, destruction, and re-creation explain why labor, marriage, death, and ritual exist as they do. Myth is etiology of the present human condition; to know origins is to know why certain hardships are structural rather than accidental. Moral teaching is embedded in the age-sequence, not appended as sermon.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: multiple world-ages end in catastrophe (flood, fire, etc.). 2) Inference: each survival selects and reshapes human capacities and customs. 3) Inference: present skills (farming, smithing, rites) are residues of those selections. 4) Inference: present evils are also residues—unfinished separations and broken taboos. 5) Conclusion: understanding destiny requires placing persons inside the long age-narrative. 6) Corollary: ritual commemorates survival logic, not mere aesthetics.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In long-term BaZi luck cycles, frame decades as “ages” with destructions and rebirths, not flat fortune scores. 2) When clients face repeated similar disasters, ask which structural pattern (not which single year) is replaying. 3) Cultivation: accept certain labors as civilizational debts, then refine them rather than fantasize exit. 4) Use flood/fire metaphors carefully in counseling as symbols of washing vs. purifying cycles. 5) Pair origin study with practical arts (craft, agriculture metaphors) for grounding practice.
entries.logic_compare: Relative to 梅葛, 查姆 is more tightly organized as multi-age etiology of culture and woe. It differs from 勒俄特依 by less emphasis on genealogical migration of a people and more on universal human condition after catastrophes. Its logic is civilizational etiology through successive worlds.

entries.logic_thesis: Meige proves that the completeness of the world depends on complementary labor across divine, human, and natural actors: creation is collaborative work, and social harmony requires each role to keep singing its part. The epic’s encyclopedic sections (creation, life, death, production) argue that knowledge is total social reproduction, not specialist theology alone. Song is the medium that binds production to meaning.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: the world and livelihood are co-made by many agents. 2) Inference: missing a craft or ritual role leaves a hole in the world. 3) Inference: teaching songs transmit role-knowledge across generations. 4) Inference: festivals and labor songs re-synchronize community with seasons. 5) Conclusion: cultural integrity is coordinated specialization under shared song-memory. 6) Corollary: individual fate is partly a role-fate within that chorus.
entries.logic_practice: 1) BaZi useful god as “role the chorus needs”—strengthen function, not vanity stars only. 2) Career advice: match chart structure to a needed social function (produce, protect, teach, mediate). 3) Cultivation: combine study with embodied craft or seasonal observance. 4) For lonely/isolated charts, prescribe communal singing/ritual work as elemental balance. 5) Diagnose family systems as multi-part polyphony; fix the missing part.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 查姆’s heavy multi-destruction frame, 梅葛 emphasizes collaborative encyclopedic completeness of life-ways. It differs from 东巴经·崇搬图 by being communal Yi song-epic rather than priestly pictographic scripture. Its logic is cooperative role-completeness sustained by song.

entries.logic_thesis: Le’eteyi proves that a people’s right to land, hierarchy, and custom is grounded in a continuous genealogical narrative from cosmic origins through migrations and branchings of lineages. Identity is not abstract ethnicity but named descent and journey. Political authority and ritual privilege follow from position on that genealogical map.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: cosmos and first beings generate lineages that split and migrate. 2) Inference: each branch’s place and power are justified by its path story. 3) Inference: forgetting genealogy dissolves claims and confuses taboos. 4) Inference: recitation of the epic is a charter for social memory. 5) Conclusion: law and belonging are functions of correctly kept origin-journey. 6) Corollary: conflict between groups is often a clash of charter narratives.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi, weight ancestral palace, year pillar, and surname/lineage context when reading roots. 2) For migration clients, read chart as journey charter—relocation as continuation of pattern, not pure escape. 3) Cultivation: write or ritually acknowledge a personal/lineage timeline as grounding practice. 4) When two remedies conflict, prefer the one coherent with family charter and land ties. 5) Use “branching” models for sibling/clan dynamics in chart comparison.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 查姆/梅葛, 勒俄特依 more strongly functions as a genealogical political charter of the Nuosu. It differs from 莫一大王 by grounding legitimacy in descent-migration rather than single anti-imperial heroics. Its logic is charter-genealogy as the spine of right.

entries.logic_thesis: Chongban Tu proves that creation and salvation are map-like processes: the world and the soul’s path are structured spaces that the Dongba can navigate with ritual diagrams and narrative. Sacred geography is operational—gates, roads, deities, and obstacles are coordinates for intervention. Knowing the map is knowing how to return what is lost (souls, order, purity).
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: the cosmos and underworld are articulated into paths and regions. 2) Inference: human misfortune is misplacement or blockage on those paths. 3) Inference: Dongba rites re-open roads, escort souls, and reinstall boundaries. 4) Inference: the scripture’s pictorial-narrative form is itself a portable map. 5) Conclusion: ritual efficacy is skilled navigation of sacred space-time. 6) Corollary: text and image are not illustration but operational cartography.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Treat BaZi as a coordinate system (time palaces, directions, stages), not a static label set. 2) For “lost soul” symptoms (dissociation, grief, shock), design path-return practices: sequential grounding rites. 3) Use directional/seasonal remedies with explicit route logic (from clash palace back to day-master). 4) Cultivation: visualization of clear gates and paths when meditating on the chart’s structure. 5) Prefer methods that specify intermediate steps over one-shot “activation.”
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Yi song epics, 崇搬图 is priestly cartographic scripture in the Dongba system. It differs from Daoist 斋醮 manuals by embedding Naxi cosmography and soul-road logistics rather than Chinese bureaucratic pantheon alone. Its logic is navigational salvation through map-rite.

entries.logic_thesis: Chen Guofu’s study proves that the Daoist canon is a historical sediment of political sponsorship, editorial programs, and sectarian agendas—not a timeless pure revelation dropped once. Authority of a text depends on its transmission path and inclusion history. Critical philology is therefore a spiritual hygiene against forged antiquity and false continuity.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Daozang contents entered through successive compilations, losses, and imperial recensions. 2) Inference: many titles’ dates and ascriptions are later constructions. 3) Inference: without stemmatics and catalog history, doctrine is misattributed. 4) Inference: correct source-criticism changes what can be claimed as “early Daoist” teaching. 5) Conclusion: historical method is necessary for truthful use of the canon. 6) Corollary: practice lineages should track text provenance as carefully as ritual secrecy.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Before basing BaZi or cultivation on a “ancient absolute,” check textual dating and corpus path. 2) Prefer methods with clear lineage + document trail over anonymous internet absolutisms. 3) When contradictions appear between classics, resolve by stratum (era/layer), not forced harmony. 4) Build a personal reading order: early strata → medieval liturgical → later synthesis. 5) Treat bibliographic notes as part of practice ethics (honesty about sources).
entries.logic_compare: Unlike narrative 中国道教史, 道藏源流考 focuses on the canon as artifact and process. It differs from 道藏分类解题 by emphasizing genesis and transmission history more than classificatory utility. Its logic is source-critical hygiene as the ground of doctrinal truth.

entries.logic_thesis: A general History of Chinese Daoism proves that Daoism is a continuous but mutating field of practices, institutions, and ideas interacting with state, popular religion, and Buddhism—not a single essence frozen in Laozi. Continuity is dialectical: new forms claim old authority while solving new social problems. Therefore “what Daoism is” must be answered period by period.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: early movements, medieval church forms, and later monastic orders differ in structure. 2) Inference: each stage responds to specific political-economic conditions. 3) Inference: doctrines are selected and rewritten under those pressures. 4) Inference: modern “Daoism” is a layered archive of those responses. 5) Conclusion: historical periodization is required for any responsible definition or practice claim. 6) Corollary: revival projects must know which layer they revive.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Locate your BaZi/Daoist method on a timeline (Han cosmology, Tang rites, Song thunder, Quanzhen inner alchemy, modern folk). 2) Avoid mixing incompatible layers without noting the join. 3) For cultivation goals, pick a period-appropriate community form (householder rite vs. monastic rule). 4) When reading omens or ethics, ask which historical Daoism is speaking. 5) Use history to deflate false “primordial” marketing of techniques.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 道藏源流考’s canon focus, this entry’s logic is institutional-intellectual periodization of the whole religion. It differs from ethnic origin epics by treating change under empire and market as normal, not as fall from a single ancestor’s teaching. Its proof is historical multiplicity under a shared name.

entries.logic_thesis: Daoist precept studies prove that liberation and ritual power are conditional on disciplined restraint: the Dao is not accessed by desire alone but by structured prohibitions that reshape body, speech, and social relation. Precepts are technologies of subject-formation, not mere moral decoration. Without precepts, techniques become predation or delusion.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: human habits generate karmic/qi turbulence that blocks clarity. 2) Inference: precepts interrupt those habits at body, mouth, and mind. 3) Inference: graded precept systems match graded initiation and office. 4) Inference: violation has both ethical and operative consequences (loss of efficacy, spirit retribution). 5) Conclusion: true method includes enforceable rule-structures. 6) Corollary: studying precept taxonomies is studying how Daoism produces trustworthy agents.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Pair any BaZi “activation” or talismanic advice with a minimum precept set (no fraud, no sexual exploitation, no reckless spirit work). 2) Design personal cultivation with measurable restraints before advanced visualization. 3) Use precept confession/renewal cycles as calendar practice tied to luck pillars. 4) When charts show strong authority/killing stars, channel them into rule-keeping roles rather than domination. 5) Evaluate teachers by their precept regime, not only charisma or accuracy.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike purely historical 中国道教史, 戒律学 isolates the normative engine inside Daoism. It differs from 三洞法服科戒文 by being a systematic academic field spanning codes, not one medieval vestment-precept text. Its logic is discipline as condition of power and truthfulness.

entries.logic_thesis: The institutional-developmental strand of Chinese Daoist historiography proves that sects, ordination systems, and temple economies are the real carriers of doctrine: ideas survive only when housed in organizations that can train, certify, and fund specialists. “Dao” in society is inseparable from corporate form. Collapse of institutions explains disappearance of methods better than metaphysical decay myths.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: movements that fail to institutionalize fragment or are absorbed. 2) Inference: successful Daoisms invent ordination, registers, temples, and patronage. 3) Inference: institutional competition with Buddhism and the state shapes liturgy and ethics. 4) Inference: later orthodoxy is the winner’s archive. 5) Conclusion: to understand a teaching’s force, map its organizational vehicle. 6) Corollary: reform must rebuild forms of transmission, not only reprint books.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Prefer learning BaZi/Daoist arts inside a living transmission structure with accountability. 2) When a technique “dies,” inspect institutional break (lineage, funding, legal status) before mystical explanations. 3) Build practice groups with clear roles, fees ethics, and training stages. 4) Read your career chart for capacity to host institutions (resource stars, officer stars). 5) Support temple/scripture conservation as cultivation of the vessel.
entries.logic_compare: This differs from the same-titled general narrative by centering corporate and economic carriers over idea-history alone. It differs from 道僧格, which is state law regulating clerics, by analyzing internal religious organization. Its logic is institutional causation of doctrinal survival.

entries.logic_thesis: The modern scholarly synthesis of Chinese Daoist history proves that objective research and insider practice can be distinguished without mutual annihilation: critical history demythologizes false claims while leaving ritual meanings intelligible as human-world-making. The “proof” is methodological: Daoism becomes speakable in public reason without being reduced to superstition or insulated from critique.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: traditional hagiography mixes fact, symbol, and legitimation. 2) Inference: modern historiography separates layers using documents, archaeology, and comparison. 3) Inference: residual patterns still show coherent religious logics (body, cosmos, bureaucracy of spirits). 4) Inference: practitioners can use cleaned history to refine rather than abandon practice. 5) Conclusion: critical knowledge is compatible with serious cultivation if roles are explicit. 6) Corollary: BaZi/Daoist fields progress by the same dual literacy.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Maintain two columns in study: historical claim vs. operative ritual claim. 2) Do not sell “Han ancient absolute” for Song-Ming techniques; label strata honestly. 3) Use academic histories to check popular BaZi myths (e.g., single origin stories). 4) Cultivation journal: note which beliefs are symbolic engines vs. empirical regularities. 5) Teach clients with transparent uncertainty bands.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 道藏源流考’s bibliographic specialization, this strand aims at whole-field public method. It differs from confessional Daoist chronicles by refusing uncritical miracle narrative as history. Its logic is dual literacy—critique and practice coexisting under explicit norms.

entries.logic_thesis: Classification-and-synopsis work on the Daozang proves that finding and using Daoist knowledge requires an epistemic map: without taxonomy (caverns, supplements, genres), the canon is an unusable labyrinth. Order of books is a theory of what kinds of knowing exist (revelation, code, ritual, alchemy, hagiography). Classification is thus a philosophical act, not clerical busywork.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: the canon is vast and heterogeneous. 2) Inference: users need genre and division keys to locate relevant methods. 3) Inference: traditional three-cavern/four-supplement schemes encode a hierarchy of authority and function. 4) Inference: modern 解题 (annotated solutions) translate that hierarchy into research paths. 5) Conclusion: access structure determines what practice can even be imagined. 6) Corollary: misclassification produces category errors in cultivation (treating fiction as code, code as lyric).
entries.logic_practice: 1) Catalog your BaZi/Daoist library by function: calendar math, image formulas, ethics, ritual, medicine. 2) Before applying a text, identify its genre and authorized use-case. 3) Build a personal “three caverns” of study: foundational theory, methods, and lived case records. 4) When stuck, climb the taxonomy (broader class) rather than random new books. 5) Write one-sentence 解题 for every technique you use—what it is for and not for.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 道藏源流考, which asks how the canon was made, 分类解题 asks how it is navigated and typed. It differs from single-scripture ethnic epics by treating multiplicity as the problem to solve. Its logic is taxonomic access as condition of correct practice.

entries.logic_thesis: The Quanzhen True Tones prove that orthodoxy of monastic Daoism is carried in melodic-rhythmic canons as much as in doctrinal prose: correct sound orders breath, emotion, and communal body into a Quanzhen subject. Liturgical music is ethical training. Wrong tones are not aesthetic failures only—they are deviations from a salvation technology.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Quanzhen communal rites require standardized vocal performance. 2) Inference: fixed 韵 (modes/formulas) synchronize the assembly’s qi and attention. 3) Inference: musical discipline embodies precepts (restraint, clarity, non-self-display). 4) Inference: transmission by ear and score preserves institutional identity across regions. 5) Conclusion: sonic form is a criterion of orthopraxy. 6) Corollary: reform of Daoism can be tracked in reform of chant.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Add breath-timed recitation to BaZi study sessions to stabilize judgment. 2) Use simple fixed chants before readings to reduce projection and greed. 3) Treat voice training as metal/water cultivation for clarity of speech in counseling. 4) When group practicing, prioritize unison formula over improvisational display. 5) Diagnose agitation as rhythmic disorder; restore with slow regular tone practice.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 道教戒律学’s legal-ethical focus, 全真正韵 locates discipline in musical performance. It differs from 大明玄教立成斋醮仪范 by being a Quanzhen sonic standard rather than a Ming state-issued complete jiao protocol. Its logic is orthodoxy-as-correct-sound.

entries.logic_thesis: This text proves that spiritual rank is publicly legible through regulated vestments and that clothing is a precept system: what one may wear is what one has vowed and been ordained to be. Appearance is not vanity but a semiotic technology of hierarchy, purity, and accountability. To wear beyond one’s grade is both legal and cosmic offense.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: the Three Caverns structure grades of scriptures and initiates. 2) Inference: each grade is paired with specific garments, colors, and ornaments. 3) Inference: vestment rules externalize inner ordination status for community policing. 4) Inference: precepts about dress prevent fraud and mixed offices. 5) Conclusion: material signs are integral to Daoist truth-procedures. 6) Corollary: ritual efficacy is tied to correct semiotic order of bodies in space.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In modern practice, define visible markers of stage (even minimal: sash, pin, seating) to prevent false authority. 2) BaZi “official/robe” imagery: read clothing and titles as responsibility loads, not loot. 3) Cultivation: keep a clean, dedicated practice garment as boundary of sacred time. 4) Refuse clients or teachers who costume as high adepts without precepts/ordination. 5) Align altar cloth colors and tools with a coherent grade logic, not random aesthetics.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike general 戒律学, this scripture specializes the precept logic into vestimentary code. It differs from 道子墨宝’s visual art treasure by being normative regulation of worn signs, not painted masterworks. Its logic is graded visibility of spiritual office.

entries.logic_thesis: Daozi’s ink corpus (as treasured Daoist visual tradition) proves that sacred presence can be stabilized in brush-traces: the image is a site where cosmic movement, deity character, and viewer’s mind co-arise. Skillful depiction is a form of theological argument in lines and voids. Seeing correctly becomes a contemplative method continuous with ritual visualization.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Daoist practice already uses inner images of gods and landscapes. 2) Inference: masterly external painting trains and corrects those inner images. 3) Inference: brush energy (骨气) models how qi moves in body and world. 4) Inference: treasured scrolls function as portable foci for devotion and study. 5) Conclusion: visual art is an epistemic organ of Daoism, not decoration. 6) Corollary: bad images miseducate desire and produce wrong spirit relations.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Use high-quality deity/cosmos images in meditation that match classical iconography. 2) Practice brush or careful diagram-drawing of BaZi structures to embody relationships. 3) Treat empty space in composition as yin training—don’t overfill charts or altars. 4) When teaching, prefer clear structural diagrams over ornate clutter. 5) Periodically purify or retire damaged sacred images rather than keep corrupted foci.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 全真正韵 (sound) and 法服科戒文 (clothing), 道子墨宝 locates formation in painted/ink vision. It differs from Dongba pictorial scripture by belonging to Chinese brush aesthetics and pantheon iconography. Its logic is theological cognition through ink-trace.

entries.logic_thesis: The Tang Daoist-Buddhist clerical statutes prove that the state claims meta-jurisdiction over religious specialists: ordination quotas, conduct, and penalties define the legal conditions under which transcendence may be publicly practiced. Holiness does not exempt one from administrative order; rather, the empire codes holiness into manageable offices. Religion’s social existence is always already legal.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: clerics occupy special economic and status positions. 2) Inference: the state fears fraud, tax-escape, and political organizing under sacred cover. 3) Inference: 道僧格 sets crimes, evidence, and punishments specific to Daoists and monks. 4) Inference: internal precepts and external law interact as dual constraints. 5) Conclusion: historical Daoist life must be read through legal status, not only mysticism. 6) Corollary: modern practitioners still inherit the problem of public accountability.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Keep practice businesses legally clean (contracts, advertising claims, tax, consent). 2) BaZi advice involving law/official stars should include real legal compliance steps. 3) Cultivation ethics: treat state law as a coarse precept layer when it protects non-harm. 4) Study how ordination/certification claims would stand under scrutiny—avoid false titles. 5) When reading historical methods, adjust for the legal environment that shaped them.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 道教戒律学’s internal religious codes, 道僧格 is imperial positive law over clerics. It differs from 大明玄教立成斋醮仪范, which standardizes liturgy as state-supported orthopraxy, by emphasizing criminal-administrative control. Its logic is state meta-rule as condition of public religion.

entries.name_han: 大明玄教立成斋醮仪范
entries.logic_thesis: The Ming “established complete” zhai-jiao manual proves that political authority can fix a standard ritual protocol to unify Daoist public worship: orthodoxy is operationalized as repeatable ceremony under court-recognized form. Efficacy and legitimacy are made to coincide with procedural completeness. Empire and altar share one administrative aesthetics of order.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: diverse local rites risk heterodoxy and disorder. 2) Inference: the Ming court sponsors a model liturgy for zhai and jiao. 3) Inference: sequence, roles, documents, and offerings are standardized. 4) Inference: priests gain recognition by performing the established form. 5) Conclusion: ritual centralization is a technology of religious and political unity. 6) Corollary: “complete” (立成) means closed protocol—authority by procedural closure.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Design personal or temple rites with clear opening–middle–closing completeness. 2) For BaZi annual rites (太岁, etc.), use fixed checklists rather than improvisation under anxiety. 3) Cultivation: treat procedural fidelity as sincerity, not empty form. 4) When comparing methods, ask which protocol is “established” by what authority. 5) Balance standard form with local need—know when you deviate and why.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 全真正韵’s monastic musical canon, this is a state-compiled complete jiao protocol for public Daoism. It differs from 道僧格 by prescribing how to worship rather than how clerics are punished. Its logic is imperial standardization of ritual as orthodoxy.
